verses.1: So if there is any comfort in Christ, any affection of love, any fellowship of the Spirit, any tenderness and compassion,
verses.2: complete my joy by thinking the same way, having the same love, being united in spirit, and thinking one thing,
verses.3: not acting in rivalry or conceit, but humbling yourselves, each regarding the other as better than yourselves,
verses.4: not looking to your own interests, but also to the interests of others.
verses.5: Let this mind be in you that was also in Christ Jesus,
verses.6: who, although he existed in the form of God, did not consider equality with God something to be seized,
verses.7: but emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, becoming like human beings; and being found in appearance as a human,
verses.8: he humbled himself, becoming obedient to the point of death, even death on a cross.
verses.9: Therefore God also highly exalted him and gave him the name above every name,
verses.10: so that at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, in heaven and on earth and under the earth,
verses.11: and every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.
verses.12: So then, beloved, just as you have always obeyed, not only when I was present, but now even more when I am absent, work out your own salvation with fear and trembling,
verses.13: for it is God who is at work in you both to will and to do for his good pleasure.
verses.14: Do all things without grumbling or disputing,
verses.15: so that you may be blameless and pure, children of God without blemish in a crooked and perverse generation, in which you appear as lights in the world,
verses.16: holding fast the word of life, so that in the day of Christ I may have reason to glory, because I did not run or toil in vain.
verses.17: But even if I am being poured out as a drink offering upon the sacrifice and service of your faith, I rejoice and share my joy with all of you.
verses.18: And you too should rejoice and share my joy.
verses.19: I hope in the Lord Jesus to send Timothy to you soon, so that I too may be encouraged by news of you.
verses.20: For I have no one else of kindred spirit who will genuinely care for your welfare,
verses.21: for all look out for their own interests, not those of Jesus Christ.
verses.22: But you know his proven worth, for he has served as a son with me in the gospel.
verses.23: So I hope to send him as soon as I see how things go with me.
verses.24: But I have confidence in the Lord that I myself also will come soon.
verses.25: I considered it necessary to send Epaphroditus, my brother and fellow worker and fellow soldier, and your apostle and minister in my service,
verses.26: for he longed for all of you and was distressed because you heard he was ill.
verses.27: For indeed he was ill, nearly to death. But God had mercy on him, not only on him but also on me, so that I would not have sorrow upon sorrow.
verses.28: Therefore I sent him all the more eagerly, so that when you see him again you may rejoice, and I may be less sorrowful.
verses.29: So welcome him in the Lord with all joy, and honor such people,
verses.30: for he was close to death because of the work of Christ, risking his life to supply what was lacking in your service to me.

notes:
Notes
- v. 6: "equality with God" reflects the translation of "ἴσα θεῷ" as a comparative construction rather than a literal "being equal to God."
- v. 11: "Lord" for "κύριος" reflects its usage as a title for Jesus, consistent with the gospel tradition.
